locations.name: Cadaques
locations.description: Whitewashed, car-light village on the Cap de Creus peninsula. One of the most architecturally and atmospherically distinctive towns on the Costa Brava - resists mass-tourism better than almost anywhere else on this coast. Dali's house at Portlligat is a short walk away. A strong day-trip option from the Santa Cristina base.

locations.name: Guernica (Gernika-Lumo)
locations.description: The most historically resonant town on the route. Market town in Biscay, seat of the Basque Parliament, home of the Gernikako Arbola (the ancient oak tree symbolising Basque freedoms), and the town bombed on 26 April 1937 that became the subject of Picasso's painting. A genuine half-day stop - not a drive-by.

photo.alt: Casa de Juntas and oak tree, Gernika

locations.name: Espelette
locations.description: French Basque village famous for the AOP piment d'Espelette. A short detour off the D918 between San Sebastian and Biarritz. The Espelette pepper cooperative sells directly - a tin is one of the most useful camp-cooking buys on the whole trip. The village turns red in late summer when peppers hang to dry from every facade. Worth 45 minutes.

photo.alt: Piment d'Espelette drying on facades in Espelette

locations.name: Camping Bachoc a la Ferme Pays Basque
locations.description: Farm-based campground in the French Basque countryside, rated 4.8. Quieter, more personal, less polished-touristic than the alternatives. One of the strongest hidden-gem matches on the whole route - the kind of small, family-run camp that fits the Snow Peak / Basecamps / wecamp sensibility without the brand. Good access to the French Basque coast (Guethary, Biarritz, Saint-Jean-de-Luz) and bus/train access back to San Sebastian as a day trip.

locations.name: Parc Jouvet
locations.description: Large riverside city park in Valence with a big playground, a mini steam train, and a small enclosure with sheep and goats. Ideal mid-drive stretch break for kids on the Aix -> Provence leg - shaded, clean, free, with fountains and a playground rated 4.6 by thousands of families.

locations.name: Glaces de Maitre Artisan
locations.description: Tiny artisan ice cream shop on Rue Jean Jaures in Arles, rated 4.9 - unusual Provencal flavors (lavender, fig, calisson, black sesame, yuzu, cassis). A strong kid-friendly and adults-equally-happy stop for the Provence leg.

photo.alt: Arles Rue Jean Jaures artisan ice cream

locations.name: Camping Beauregard Plage
locations.description: Family-oriented campground directly on the beach in Marseillan-Plage (Bassin de Thau / Sete area). Rated 4.3 across 1200+ reviews, with premium pitches that include their own private shower and toilet. Abundant shade from pines, clean facilities, and direct beach access on one side and the resort amenities on the other. Much calmer than Cap d'Agde and much more authentic than the Sete port campgrounds. Good 2-night base for Sete market, Mont Saint-Clair viewpoint, and Bassin de Thau oysters.

editorial.summary: Best-fit family beach campground for the Sete / Bassin de Thau stop.

campground.notes: Direct beach access. Premium pitches with private bathroom available.

locations.name: Marseillan
locations.description: Small port village at the western end of the Bassin de Thau, 15 minutes from Sete and the home of Noilly Prat vermouth (free cellar tours). Small pedestrian streets, oyster bars on the quay, Tuesday morning market. Quieter and more authentic than Sete itself.

locations.name: La Fabrique a gout-the
locations.description: 4.8-rated artisan tea house / bakery in Marseillan village center. Home-made sandwiches, bagels, cookies, brownies, pancakes, and thoughtful breakfast selection - strong option for family brunch or picnic supplies before a beach day. Open 8am-6pm most days, closed Thursdays.

location.address: 1 Rue Achille Maffre de Bauge, 34340 Marseillan

locations.name: Chez Alphonse & Fils
locations.description: 4.8-rated hidden-gem ice cream shop on Rue Grand Rue Mario Roustan in Sete - small, family-run, with original Mediterranean flavors (sesame is the signature). Walkable from the Halles de Sete covered market. One stop, one ice cream each - exactly the right break for kids after provisioning.

locations.name: Olivier Bajard
locations.description: High-end French patissier's Collioure shop - world-class chocolates, glaces, and savoury lunch options. Perfect lunch-pastry stop on the Marseillan -> Santa Cristina drive, 5 minutes walk from Collioure's painted harbour.

locations.name: Casa Flora Girona
locations.description: 4.8-rated restaurant in Girona's old town, run by a local couple - fresh, well-balanced three-course menu for around 25EUR that regularly beats much more expensive options. Small, intimate, recommended by local guides. Perfect lunch stop on the SC -> Barcelona drive (or on a SC base day Girona trip).

photo.alt: Girona old town near Casa Flora

locations.name: El Palmeral de Elche
locations.description: UNESCO World Heritage palm grove in Elche - 200,000+ date palms descended from Arab irrigation systems. Vast shade, clean playgrounds, fountains, benches, public bathrooms. The single best mid-drive kid stop on the Valencia -> Cabo de Gata leg. Free entry, open 7am-11pm. Walking loop 1-3h depending on pace. 4.6 rating, 17,000+ reviews - consistently praised as family-perfect.

photo.alt: Palmeral de Elche UNESCO palm grove

family.notes: Shaded palm grove with playgrounds - ideal mid-drive family rest.

Right at the Mediterranean. Good 1-night stop to break the Valencia -> Cabo de Gata leg and visit Cartagena as a half-day trip.

locations.description: 4.9-rated hidden-gem gelateria in Cartagena's old town on Calle Jabonerias. Creamy, generous scoops, English-speaking staff, slushies and coffee too. Perfect afternoon break while walking Cartagena's Roman theatre and old town.

photo.alt: Cartagena old town near Tiramisu gelateria

locations.name: Cartagena
locations.description: Ancient Mediterranean port city, founded by the Carthaginians, later a major Roman city. Walkable old town with a visible Roman Theatre, naval history museum, Modernista architecture, and strong seafood tradition. A surprisingly authentic Spanish coastal city - not touristy. Good half-day visit between Lo Monte and Cabo de Gata.

locations.name: Camping Caceres
locations.description: Well-run 129-pitch campground ~2km west of Caceres UNESCO old town, rated 4.4 with 3,400+ reviews. Each pitch has its own private sanitary block (shower, toilet, washbasin) - unusual and excellent. Pool, restaurant, good WiFi, bus stop opposite the gate into town. Strong 2-night base for the Extremadura leg.

photo.alt: Caceres old town near Camping Caceres

campground.notes: Private sanitary block per pitch. Bus into Caceres old town opposite the gate.

locations.name: Caceres old town (Ciudad Monumental)
locations.description: UNESCO World Heritage walled old town - one of the most complete medieval and Renaissance town centers in Europe. Stork nests on every tower, stone lanes, small plazas, Arab, Moorish, Roman and Jewish layers. Very walkable with kids. The Plaza Mayor just outside the walls is a great dinner stop.

locations.name: Borona Bistro
locations.description: 4.9-rated modern Spanish bistro in Caceres old town - tasting menu with wine pairings, consistently described as one of the best meals on any Extremadura trip. Small, intimate, professional service. Book ahead.

locations.name: Trujillo
locations.description: Hilltop conquistador town between Caceres and Monfrague. Plaza Mayor with the equestrian statue of Pizarro, medieval castle, storks on every roof. Smaller and quieter than Caceres, very photogenic, easy half-day with kids.

locations.name: Restaurante Dos Orillas Trujillo
locations.description: 4.7-rated restaurant hidden in Trujillo's old center, with a stunning plant-filled courtyard that stays several degrees cooler than outdoors. Perfect lunch stop on the Caceres base day or on the way to Salamanca. Small seasonal menu, local ingredients, very attentive staff.

locations.name: Parque Nacional de Monfrague
locations.description: Spain's most important raptor reserve - Griffon vultures, Egyptian vultures, black vultures, Bonelli's eagles, Spanish imperial eagles, black storks. The Salto del Gitano viewpoint gives eye-level views of nesting vultures across the Tagus gorge. A genuine wildlife-watching experience kids remember. 30km from Caceres - makes a half-day trip or a waypoint on the way to Salamanca.

location.address: Parque Nacional de Monfrague, 10695 Torrejon el Rubio
